correctness.rationale: The exact ODE yields N_i∞=N_i0(1-q_i z_i) and h=KΦ_q(1-s exp(-h)). Positive intercept and strict concavity give a unique positive fixed point; the Jacobian satisfies Jh<h, so rho(J)<1. Differentiation gives dz_i/dq_j=(1-z_i)w_j[(I-J)^(-1)K]_ij. The Neumann series has positive terms exactly on directed positive-length transmission paths. Finite numerical tests are supplementary and do not replace the general analytic argument.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a complete, structurally motivated dichotomy for whether a fatal-outcome change in one subpopulation affects infection in another at unchanged infectious duration and next-generation threshold. Directed reachability determines exact zero versus strictly positive effects; the sensitivity resolvent quantifies indirect transmission-walk amplification. This enables mathematically precise comparison of two epidemiological model normalizations without implying a clinical intervention.
